answer.generated: The two key characteristics of paging and segmentation that signify a fundamental breakthrough in memory management, as compared to fixed and dynamic partitioning, are their ability to provide more flexible and efficient memory allocation and management. Specifically, paging allows for the division of the logical address space into fixed-size pages, which can be mapped to non-contiguous physical frames, thus enabling better utilization of memory resources. Segmentation, on the other hand, divides the logical address space into variable-sized segments, each with its own protection and access attributes, thereby enhancing the security and organization of data. These characteristics fundamentally shift the approach to memory management by introducing a more granular and adaptable method for handling memory allocation, surpassing the limitations of fixed and dynamic partitioning methods.
